comment: Four classes over three defects, all found by an adversarial pass that worked
from the invariants and asked PostgreSQL what it accepts, rather than from the
tests. None of them was caught by five phases of campaigns, because every
campaign attacks the rules that were written and these were rules that were not.
A0 and A1 are the same rule at its two levels: refused where the branch is handed
over, and refused again by the writer as a floor. A2 and A3 are two defects that
concealed each other — a hoisted WITH made an undeclared reference resolve, so
the statement worked and neither showed.
Every killer runs in the root module or in internal/expr and needs no database.
The server's own answers are in internal/gendemo/m16_unionorder_test.go.
evidence_commit_note: ab3e1df is the revision every UNION ALL class was last applied to and run at, in a
worktree checked out at exactly that commit, with the manifests read and written
outside it so the tree stayed clean between classes. It is kept reachable as
The five UNION ALL campaigns were rerun together at one revision after `mutate
anchors` found four anchors that later phases had silently invalidated by editing
the code they quote. An anchor that no longer matches makes its class look like a
survivor, so the campaigns were pinned to revisions where they no longer ran.
They run again, and three harness controls were active: anchors still quote their
code, every site names the function its anchor is inside, and each semantic probe
survives every mutation in another function.

classes.name: A branch carrying a locking clause is accepted when the branch is handed over

expresses: The construction-time refusal stops firing, so a branch that locks the rows it
reads reaches the compound. PostgreSQL refuses a locking clause anywhere in a
set operation, parentheses included, so the statement can only ever fail — and
it fails at the server rather than where the branch was given.

note: The writer keeps the same check as a floor, so the mutant still fails to render
— with the writer's diagnostic and at the wrong moment. The killer asserts the
diagnostic, which is what distinguishes the authority from the floor.
This class exists because the audit found the defect, not because the rule was
planned: needsParens listed the locking clauses among the things parentheses fix,
and PostgreSQL refuses them parenthesised.
The probe asserts the mistake is recorded on the builder, not that the
statement fails to render. It was the second when the campaign first ran it,
and the writer's floor made it pass under the mutant.
The killer asserts "UNION ALL branch" and not only the sentence. Both refusals
carry the same sentence, because they call the same function, and only the
wrapping says which one spoke: the builder names the operation and the writer
names the position. Without that the class survived, with the floor doing the
work the authority was supposed to be doing.

classes.name: The writer stops refusing a locked branch

expresses: The floor is removed: a compound assembled inside the package, bypassing the
builder, renders a locking clause the server will not take.

note: Probe and killer are the compiler's own refusal list, because a floor has no
level above it: the public route is A0's, and it is refused before this runs.

classes.name: A branch's own WITH is written bare

expresses: A branch carrying a WITH clause stops being parenthesised. In the first branch
PostgreSQL accepts the result and hoists the declaration to the whole compound,
so it is evaluated once for the operation and visible to every branch; in any
later branch it is a syntax error. The same omission fails loudly in one
position and silently in the other, which is why the silent one had stood.

note: The killer asserts all three positions, because the hoisting is only observable
in the first: the later ones stop compiling and would be caught by anything.

classes.name: A named query can be selected from without being declared

expresses: A reference to a named query nothing declared is written as a bare identifier,
so the statement names a relation that does not exist. It reads correctly and
fails at the server.
This is the defect that let a branch borrow another branch's CTE: with the
declaration hoisted by A2's defect, the borrowed name resolved and the
statement worked, which is why neither showed up on its own.

note: The killer is the scope claim rather than the reference rule, because the claim
is what the compiler has asserted in a comment since the compound node was
written and what was false until both defects were fixed.

classes.name: The operation's own named queries do not reach the statement

expresses: The items declared on the operation are dropped on the way to the tree, so
the branches that read them select from a named query nothing declares.
This is the capability that had to exist before a branch's WITH could be
parenthesised. Sharing a named query between branches used to work because
the declaration was hoisted out of the first branch; closing that without
opening this would have removed the only way to do it.

note: The probe and the precondition are one assertion: what makes the mutation
observable is exactly that the items reach the tree. The killer is a level up,
at the statement, where the declaration has to be in front of the operation and
written once rather than once per branch.
